name: Plasma cell
markers: No CD20; little CD19 or surface antibody
BLIMP-1 and XBP1 (inside the cell; master regulators)
summary: An antibody factory: the last stage of a B cell, with an off-centre nucleus and cytoplasm packed with endoplasmic reticulum. It makes thousands of antibody molecules a second. Short-lived plasma cells act for days near the site of a response. Long-lived ones settle in the bone marrow and can secrete antibody for years.
functions: Arises from an activated B cell either straight away, outside the follicle (a first wave of mostly IgM, lasting days), or later from a germinal centre (higher-affinity, class-switched antibody). Dividing precursors, plasmablasts, appear in human blood about a week after infection or vaccination.

Secretes the soluble form of the antibody its B cell carried: IgM, IgG, IgA or IgE. IgG neutralises toxins and viruses and coats microbes for engulfment, IgA protects mucosal surfaces, and IgE arms mast cells and basophils.
Settles where it can survive: in the lymph node medulla for days to weeks, in mucosal tissue (for IgA), or in the bone marrow, to which it travels through the blood following CXCL12.

Is kept alive in bone marrow niches by survival signals such as IL-6, APRIL and BAFF, which it senses through BCMA. Long-lived plasma cells there keep antibody levels up for years, and antibody levels against viruses such as measles and mumps are estimated to last for decades in humans.
Debated: which cells build the bone marrow niche for long-lived plasma cells (eosinophils, megakaryocytes and stromal cells have all been proposed). Most of this evidence comes from mice.
Debated: whether long-lived plasma cells truly live for years on their own or are topped up by memory B cells that are stimulated continually without antigen.
Has lost most of its surface antibody and its MHC class II, so it no longer responds to antigen or presents it. It does not divide once fully mature.
abundance: Very rare in healthy human blood. Plasmablasts rise to a few percent of B cells about a week after infection or vaccination. In human bone marrow, plasma cells are roughly 1% of nucleated cells. Most numbers on long-lived plasma cells come from mice.
